market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Midday Thu Oct 22 (~9:00 AM PT), ~2.5h into the regular session: Dow -0.4% to -0.5%, S&P 500 -1.4% (morning low 7,646), Nasdaq -2.3% testing 26,000 (IBD live); QQQ -2.35% (708.20), SPY -1.27% (763.30). Sharp split under the surface: equal-weight RSP +0.18% while the cap-weighted AI complex bleeds - SOXX -5.9%, Roundhill memory ETF -5.5%, MAGS -2.5% - as defensives (PG, LLY, SPOT, CRM, AAPL) run green. Two morning 'fake V' rebounds were sold back down within minutes. VIX was 18.1 at 7 AM PT and has not been seen above 20; fear is concentrated in AI/leverage names, not the broad index (r/wallstreetbets daily sentiment).
market_snapshot.notes: Thursday Oct 22, 9:00am PT - midday, 2.5 hours into the regular session. The selloff held but stopped deepening: Nasdaq -2.3%, S&P -1.4%, Dow -0.4%. META bounced off its $648 low to trade ~-6% ($656-660); TSLA fought back from -4% to -0.85%; GOOGL fell below its 200-day (-2.4%). Semis stayed the epicenter - SOXL -17.7%, NVDA -3.9%, AMD -7.4%, MU -4.4%, with WDC -7.3% ahead of tonight's print. P&G's beat (+5.5%) anchored the defensive rotation. 10Y at 5.01% (-14 bps on the day) is the cushion. Brent ~$111-112 on the still-unconfirmed Iran-strike tape. Anthropic S-1-for-Friday still single-source.

headlines.headline: Indexes ground lower into midday: Nasdaq -2.3% testing 26,000, S&P 500 -1.4% (morning low 7,646), Dow -0.4% to -0.5%; QQQ -2.35% (708.20), SPY -1.27% (763.30) (IBD live; r/wallstreetbets daily sentiment).
headlines.why_it_matters: Two 'fake V' rebounds were sold back down within minutes - intraday bounces are being used as exits. But the equal-weight RSP holding +0.18% says this is crowded-AI deleveraging, not a broad collapse.

headlines.headline: META bounced off its intraday low but still trades -6% to -6.5% (~$656-660; low $648.26-648.37), with $650 the community's 'line in the sand'. The Class C dilution plan and uncapped capex remain the overhang, even as 13+ brokerages raised targets after the Q3 beat (Pivotal $960, TD Cowen $850 Buy, Morningstar $850 fair value).
headlines.why_it_matters: The tape is repricing who funds AI - free cash flow went negative and the non-voting share plan reads as a dilution vehicle, so the revenue beat cannot carry the stock. A close below $650 is the retail pain point to watch.

headlines.headline: TSLA reversed most early losses - from a morning low of $373.71 (down ~4%) to ~$383 (-0.85%) - as post-earnings analyst targets splintered: BofA $460 Buy, Piper $475, RBC $480 Buy, JPM $430 Neutral, UBS $425 Neutral, Goldman $360 Neutral, HSBC $157 Reduce; StoneX reiterated $475 Buy, CLSA upgraded to Hold.
headlines.why_it_matters: The tape fought off the morning dump once the beat (adj. EPS $0.48, rev $28.05B) was priced against the pushed-out autonomy timeline - the Street is now just arguing over how much the delay is worth.

headlines.headline: Alphabet slid another 2.4% midday, falling further below its 200-day moving average on the AI-capex repricing; earnings are due Oct 28 after the close (IBD live).
headlines.why_it_matters: The selloff is spreading from semis and META to the next hyperscaler print - GOOGL on Oct 28 is the next checkpoint for whether capex guidance, not results, sets the price.

headlines.headline: The AI hardware chain kept liquidating into midday: SOXX -5.9%, Roundhill memory ETF -5.5%, leveraged SOXL -17.7%; NVDA -3.9% ($213.23), AMD -7.4%, MU -4.4% ($873.10), AVGO -4.6%; optical (COHR -12.6%, LITE -10%) and power names (GEV -11.4%, VST -10.3%) hit too. WDC -7.3% and Seagate -7% ahead of tonight's Western Digital print (consensus ~$4.11 EPS on ~$4.16B revenue).
headlines.why_it_matters: Lam's in-line outlook set the template - anything short of a demand beat now reads as a cap. Tonight's WDC guide is the number that moves memory.

headlines.headline: Micron's Taoyuan DRAM fab faces a 24-hour strike (9am Thu to 9am Fri Taiwan time) as the union demands a long-term profit-sharing mechanism; the scale of participation and any output impact are unconfirmed (FinanceFeeds, citing TradingKey/CNA). Micron settled separately with its Taichung union on Oct 21.
headlines.why_it_matters: Memory is already the tape's weakest link - a supply event at a major DRAM fab could reprice chips on a different axis entirely. Participation and impact unconfirmed - single-source, treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: FRESH: Procter & Gamble beat - fiscal Q1 net sales $23.28B (+4%, vs ~$22.8B est), organic sales +4% on 2.4% volume growth, core EPS $2.00 vs $1.89; stock +5.5% to +6%. Raised all-in FY sales guide to 2-4% on the Thorne acquisition but flagged a $1.4B commodity headwind (up from $1.0B).
headlines.why_it_matters: A clean defensive beat on a risk-off day - staples are absorbing the rotation out of AI hardware, which is exactly why the equal-weight index is green while the cap-weighted one bleeds.

headlines.headline: Anthropic S-1 watch: Seeking Alpha and PYMNTS now echo Yahoo Finance's three-source report that Anthropic could publicly file its S-1 as soon as Friday, clearing the 15-day runway for a November listing; the company declined to comment. Valuation chatter has slipped toward ~$1.5T from ~$2T; the WSJ reported H1 revenue of $16.3B and a net loss over $80B.
headlines.why_it_matters: The largest-ever IPO would land right into an AI-spending selloff - a confirmed filing refocuses the tape on AI unit economics. Still one originating report, now syndicated - single-source, unconfirmed, treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: SpaceX round-tripped its earnings pop: -5.3% to -6% (~$150.92) after Wednesday's 8% jump on its first quarterly profit. Boards of TSLA and SpaceX have formed committees to explore a merger - no deal agreed.
headlines.why_it_matters: A full round-trip on the earnings pop shows the tape punishing anything priced on the AI/Musk narrative. TSLA's relative strength against SPCX reads as merger-arb rotation into the cheaper name.

headlines.headline: WTI ~$98.35 (+1%+), Brent ~$111-112 near a five-month high, on the unconfirmed NYT report of planned U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms. Trump said the U.S. is 'not currently negotiating'; Iran's foreign minister signaled openness to diplomacy; Reuters reported more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.
headlines.why_it_matters: Energy is the one real bid - if the strike tape proves out, crude becomes the macro risk factor into year-end; the cause is still unconfirmed, so today's oil bid can fade fast. Single-source on the cause - treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to ~5.01% (-14 bps on the day) as investors fled to safety; TLT +1.36%. France's 10-year hit its highest since 2002, China's CSI 300 entered bear-market territory, and Asian markets fell 3%+.
headlines.why_it_matters: Bond and equity desks agree on one thing - fear. Falling long yields cushion equity multiples, but today's bid is flight, not growth optimism.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning. Carried: Q3 cash distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized) is set for payment Nov 6 to unitholders of record Oct 26; Q3 results release before market open on Nov 3 with an 11:00 AM ET call. October 1: 8-K disclosed 34.5M new Class A units (9.25% fixed distribution rate) issued to J-W Energy in a private reorganization.

watch_next: After the close: Western Digital (and Bloom Energy) earnings - the next AI memory/supply-chain checkpoint; consensus ~$4.11 EPS on ~$4.16B revenue.
Friday: Anthropic S-1 filing watch (still single-source, unconfirmed); S&P Global flash October PMIs.
Rest of the session: whether dip-buyers show into the close or semis drag lower - QQQ 707 and SPX 7650/7642 are the levels, with 200-day supports well below.
Crude tape: WTI ~$98, Brent ~$111-112; U.S.-Israel Iran strike-plans reporting unconfirmed - treat as fragile.
Fed blackout into the Oct 28 decision; December hike the unanimous economist expectation (Reuters poll, carried). GOOGL earnings Oct 28 after the close.
analysis: What changed since the 8:00 AM PT post-open brief: the selloff stopped deepening but refused to reverse. META climbed off its $648 low to trade ~-6% ($656-660), TSLA fought back from -4% to -0.85%, and the Nasdaq held -2.3% while the Dow stayed down just -0.4% to -0.5%. Two intraday 'fake V' rebounds were sold within minutes - the tape's dominant pattern is distribution into strength. The day's real story is the split underneath: equal-weight RSP +0.18% green while the cap-weighted AI complex bleeds (SOXX -5.9%, SOXL -17.7%, DRAM -5.5%, MAGS -2.5%), with P&G's clean beat (+5.5-6%) anchoring a genuine defensive rotation (LLY, SPOT, CRM, NOW, AAPL all green). New since 8 AM: GOOGL slid below its 200-day (-2.4%) ahead of Oct 28 earnings, SpaceX fully round-tripped its earnings pop, Micron's Taoyuan strike added a supply wildcard to memory, and the Anthropic S-1 report got syndicated (still single-source). Signal vs noise: META's dilution-driven repricing and the hardware-chain liquidation (LRCX in-line read as a cap, WDC -7% pre-print) are signal - the market has moved from 'who grows in AI' to 'who pays for AI'. The Iran-strike oil bid and the NBIS/SpaceX-unlock rumors are noise until confirmed. The TSLA intraday recovery is ambiguous - merger-arb rotation, not fundamentals. The 10Y at 5.01% is the day's real offset, but it's a fear bid, not a growth bid.

community_signals.takeaway: Near-capitulation on the AI trade but not the broad index: consensus is that Wall Street now cares only about capex and free cash flow, not revenue/EPS; META's +7%-after-hours-to-6% reversal is the emblem of 'good earnings, falling stock'; $650 is the community's 'line in the sand'. Fear/greed ~25/100 with VIX still under 20 - bears note SPY is only 3% off its ATH and call it 'an ant-sized pullback', framing it as crowded-AI deleveraging rather than a crash. TSLA's rally from 374 to 388 read as merger-arb rotation from SPCX; tonight's WDC/BE prints are the hoped-for 'rescue'.
